name: MMStar
description: An elite vision-indispensable multi-modal benchmark comprising 1,500 samples meticulously selected by humans. MMStar benchmarks 6 core capabilities and 18 detailed axes, aiming to evaluate LVLMs' multi-modal capacities with carefully balanced and purified samples.

creator.name: Lin Chen, Jinsong Li, Xiaoyi Dong, Pan Zhang, Yuhang Zang, Zehui Chen, Haodong Duan, Jiaqi Wang, Yu Qiao, Dahua Lin, Feng Zhao
creator.affiliation: University of Science and Technology of China, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, Shanghai AI Laboratory

citeAs: Lin Chen, Jinsong Li, Xiaoyi Dong, Pan Zhang, Yuhang Zang, Zehui Chen, Haodong Duan, Jiaqi Wang, Yu Qiao, Dahua Lin, Feng Zhao. Are We on the Right Way for Evaluating Large Vision-Language Models? arXiv:2403.20330v2 [cs.CV] 9 Apr 2024
rai:dataCollection: Samples are first roughly selected from current benchmarks (SEED, AI2D, ScienceQA, MMBench, MathVista, MMMU) with an automated pipeline using eight powerful LLMs as candidate inspectors for visual dependency and LLM leakage. Samples that could be answered by more than 2 of the 8 LLMs are excluded. Then 16 leading LVLMs are used to gauge the difficulty of the samples and split them into four levels (easy, moderate, hard, tough). Finally, strict manual review and selection are applied to curate 1,500 high-quality multimodal evaluation samples.
rai:dataCollectionType: Secondary Data analysis, Manual Human Curator, Software Collection
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Samples collected from six existing multi-modal benchmarks: SEED (focused on natural images), AI2D, ScienceQA, MMBench, MathVista, and MMMU (centered on scientific and technical knowledge). Initial pool of 22,401 samples.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: An automated pipeline was developed to preliminarily filter out samples that do not meet visual dependency and minimal data leakage criteria. Two closed-source LLMs (GPT4-Turbo, GeminiPro) and six open-source LLMs (sizing 20B or larger) were employed as inspectors with a 2-shot in-context inference strategy to minimize response refusals and ensure consistency in answer formatting. Only samples with hit counts of two or fewer hits (around 75% of LLM inspectors fail to provide the correct answer) were retained. This reduced the sample pool from 22,401 to 11,607. All questions were converted into a multiple-choice format.
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Three experts conducted manual review to ensure: 1) each sample's answer should be based on the understanding of visual content; 2) selected samples should cover a comprehensive range of capability assessment dimensions; 3) most samples should require LVLMs to possess advanced multi-modal abilities for resolution. To expedite manual selection, samples were split into four difficulty categories based on hit counts of 16 LVLMs: easy (12-16), moderate (8-11), hard (4-7), and tough (0-3). Final selection of 1,500 high-quality samples considered both diversity of capability dimensions and difficulty levels.
rai:dataAnnotationAnalysis: Samples were evaluated by 16 leading LVLMs to gauge difficulty and split into four difficulty levels. The hit frequency for each evaluation sample was documented during the automated filtering process.
rai:annotatorDemographics: Three experts were involved in the manual review process.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: Eight LLMs used as inspectors: GPT4-Turbo, GeminiPro, Qwen-1.5-72B, InternLM2-20B, Yi-34B, Mixtral-8x7B, Deepseek-67B, LLaMA2-70B. Sixteen LVLMs used for difficulty assessment: GPT4V, GeminiPro-Vision, LLaVA series, and others.
rai:dataReleaseMaintenancePlan: The authors plan to expand MMStar into a larger, online test set and explore dynamic evaluation methods to maintain sample visual dependency and reduce accidental data leakage into LLM's and LVLM's training corpora.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The benchmark addresses two critical issues in LVLM evaluation: 1) Visual content is unnecessary for many samples in existing benchmarks, and 2) Unintentional data leakage exists in LLM and LVLM training. These problems lead to misjudgments of actual multi-modal gains and potentially misguide the study of LVLM.
rai:dataBiases: The paper identifies that existing benchmarks contain samples where visual content is unnecessary - answers can be directly inferred from questions and options, or from world knowledge embedded in LLMs. For example, more than 50% of ScienceQA questions and 20% of MMMU questions can be solved by most LLMs directly without visual input.
rai:dataLimitations: The benchmark consists of 1,500 samples, which is relatively small compared to some existing benchmarks. The samples are derived from existing benchmarks, which may limit the diversity of evaluation scenarios. The manual review process involved only three experts. Even with careful curation, no LVLMs managed to reach a passing average score (60%) in the core capabilities of fine-grained perception, logical reasoning, science & technology, and mathematics, highlighting these dimensions as particularly challenging.
rai:dataUseCases: Testing and evaluation of Large Vision-Language Models (LVLMs). The benchmark is designed to evaluate LVLMs' multi-modal capabilities across 6 core capabilities (Coarse Perception, Fine-grained Perception, Instance Reasoning, Logical Reasoning, Science & Technology, Mathematics) and 18 detailed axes. Usage guidelines emphasize that samples should only be answered based on understanding visual content, with minimal data leakage and requiring advanced multi-modal capabilities.
